snes9x.optimization: -O3 -flto -DNDEBUG on CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS (compile) AND LDFLAGS (link). The earlier build cleared LTO and added no link-time -O, so Emscripten's link/codegen step shipped an effectively unoptimized core — the dominant cause of the on-device FPS cap. Rebuilt with aggressive optimization: .wasm 3347860 -> 2910410 bytes (~13% smaller). -flto (full, not thin) linked cleanly.

build_command: emmake make platform=emscripten PROFILE=<accuracy|balanced|performance> -j$(nproc)  # with ALL object files deleted between profiles — make does not track the PROFILE_* define change, so a stale tree silently produces a mislabelled core

optimization_pass.what_was_actually_wrong: The previous metadata in this file implied the bsnes cores were built with the same aggressive flags as snes9x. They were not. Correction, verified by dumping the real command lines: CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS DID already carry -O3, supplied by the generic Makefile block `ifeq ($(DEBUG),0) FLAGS += -O3` (DEBUG=0 at Makefile:1) which is folded in via `CXXFLAGS += $(FLAGS)`. The emscripten PLATFORM block adds no -O of its own, which is what a grep of that block shows, but the generic block downstream supplies it. The REAL defect was on the LINK side: `LDFLAGS += $(fpic) $(SHARED)` never receives $(FLAGS), so the Emscripten link ran at its -O0 default. Under Emscripten that is severe — the link runs wasm-opt over the whole module AND is where the ASYNCIFY instrumentation pass executes, so at -O0 wasm-opt was skipped entirely, the Asyncify-instrumented module shipped with no post-instrumentation cleanup, -s ASSERTIONS defaulted to 1, and the JS glue was never minified (254,534 B of unminified loader, vs snes9x's 69,292 B — the visible tell). There was also no -DNDEBUG anywhere, so bsnes/nall assert() was live in the hot CPU/PPU/SMP paths.
optimization_pass.isolated_effect_of_link_optimization: Adding ONLY `-O3` to the link, compile flags untouched: .wasm 3,724,182 -> 1,838,476 bytes (-50.6%), JS loader 254,534 -> 95,962 bytes (-62%), accuracy 60.09 -> 46.18 ms/frame liftoff and 39.38 -> 34.99 ms/frame TurboFan. So the missing link-time -O was worth roughly half the module size, and it is where nearly all of the accuracy profile's measurable speed gain came from.
optimization_pass.final_link_flags: -O3 -msimd128 -s ASSERTIONS=0 -s SAFE_HEAP=0 -s STACK_OVERFLOW_CHECK=0 -s RUNTIME_DEBUG=0 --closure 1 -s WASM=1 -s ALLOW_TABLE_GROWTH=1 -s ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1 -s INITIAL_MEMORY=100663296 -s STACK_SIZE=8388608 -s ASYNCIFY=1 -s ASYNCIFY_STACK_SIZE=524288 -s MODULARIZE=1 -s EXPORT_ES6=1 -s EXPORT_NAME=<name> -s INVOKE_RUN=0 -s EXIT_RUNTIME=0 -s ERROR_ON_UNDEFINED_SYMBOLS=0 -s ENVIRONMENT=web,worker,node -s EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS=<22 retro_* + malloc/free> -s EXPORTED_RUNTIME_METHODS=<ccall,cwrap,addFunction,removeFunction,setValue,getValue,UTF8ToString,stringToUTF8,HEAPU8,HEAPU16,HEAP32,HEAPU32,HEAPF64>
optimization_pass.no_debug_flags: Confirmed: no -g, no -gsource-map, no -sDEMANGLE_SUPPORT on any compile or link line.
optimization_pass.wasm_export_names_now_minified: SIDE EFFECT WORTH KNOWING: because the link now runs at -O3, Emscripten minifies the wasm module's own export names (the .wasm reports 53 single-letter exports instead of readable retro_* symbols). Nothing in the app depends on raw wasm export names — tas-engine.js goes through the JS glue via Module.cwrap/ccall — and this was verified: all 20 raw retro_* entry points plus _malloc/_free are present as Module._retro_* on every profile, all 13 EXPORTED_RUNTIME_METHODS resolve, and retro_cheat_set/retro_cheat_reset appear ZERO times in either the wasm or the JS glue of all three cores. Only tooling that greps the .wasm for literal retro_* strings would notice.
optimization_pass.reproducible: Two independent clean builds of PROFILE=accuracy produced byte-identical output (wasm sha256 3d98de4ade6e772640e8172f88f418726f6ce16abba44ed097811d5d9e3aafd0).

measurements.how: node tools/run-smoke.mjs <core.js> 300 against the real committed ROM (assets/Super Mario All-Stars (USA).sfc); ms/frame is the harness's own `ran retro_run() x300 in Nms` divided by 300. Run-to-run noise measured at about 2%, so differences under ~2% are not meaningful.
measurements.two_v8_tiers: run-smoke re-execs Node under --liftoff-only (baseline WASM compiler) to dodge a historical V8 TurboFan crash on these large ASYNCIFY modules, which UNDER-REPORTS optimized builds. Setting __RUNSMOKE_REEXEC=1 skips that re-exec and measures on the optimizing tier. On Node 22.23.2 TurboFan NO LONGER crashes on any of these cores (old or new), so both numbers are reported. Neither is the final judge — real on-device iOS Safari FPS is.

accuracy.delta: wasm -51.6%, js -85.1%, liftoff -22.1% (1.28x faster), turbofan -9.2% (1.10x faster)

performance.delta: wasm -51.6%, js -85.1%, liftoff -69.2% (3.24x faster), turbofan -67.5% (3.08x faster)

balanced.delta: NEW profile. 7.5x cheaper per frame than accuracy while still bsnes-derived.

measurements.why_accuracy_barely_moved: The asymmetry (performance 3.1x faster, accuracy only 1.10x) is real and explained. A -DLIBCO_SWAP_COUNTER diagnostic build counted libco/Asyncify fiber swaps per emulated frame: accuracy 39,436/frame, balanced 1,265/frame, performance 542/frame. Each swap is an emscripten_fiber_swap, i.e. a full Asyncify unwind + rewind, costing roughly 1.15 us. At ~39.4k swaps/frame that alone accounts for essentially the entire 45 ms frame. So the accuracy profile is bottlenecked on fiber-swap FREQUENCY, not on codegen quality — which is exactly why link-time optimization halved its size but barely moved its speed, while the performance profile (73x fewer swaps) was dominated by the removable codegen overhead and got 3.1x faster. Reaching 60 FPS (16.6 ms/frame) with 39.4k swaps/frame would need ~0.4 us/swap, which Asyncify cannot deliver. The only real levers are fewer swaps (that is what the balanced and performance profiles do) or a VM-native stack-switching primitive (JSPI), and iOS Safari does not support JSPI. Recommend the new `balanced` core for near-60-FPS bsnes-grade work and keep `accuracy` as the paused/frame-advance reference.

asyncify_pruning_rejected.ground_truth: -s ASYNCIFY_ADVISE=1 on an otherwise-final build. Asyncify instruments 1212 distinct functions. Only ONE import can change state: emscripten_fiber_swap. The real swap chain is emscripten_fiber_swap <- co_switch / co_fiber_entry <- the SuperFamicom + GameBoy schedulers and CPU/SMP/PPU/DSP/coprocessor code. Reason breakdown: 994 'due to initial scan' (i.e. the function contains an INDIRECT call), 518 via a named callee, 1 import. Cluster breakdown: Processor::GSU 431, Processor::R65816 363, SuperFamicom::* 236, nall::function<> thunks 90, GameBoy::* 35, Processor::SPC700 17, Processor::LR35902 10, Processor::ARM 5, plus ~60 non-emulation (printf/stdio/RTTI/file-I-O/std::vector/resampler).
asyncify_pruning_rejected.why_it_looks_prunable_but_is_not: 82% of the instrumented set exists only because of indirect calls, which is exactly what ASYNCIFY_IGNORE_INDIRECT removes. But bsnes reaches its fiber swap THROUGH indirect calls: Processor::R65816::op_* dispatch VIRTUALLY to SuperFamicom::CPU::op_read, which calls co_switch; and the entire bus map is nall::function<> lambdas (SuperFamicom::Bus::map_reset()::$_0, SuperFamicom::CPU::enable()::$_0). Those indirect call sites are ON the unwind path.

BROKEN, and worse — threw 'null function or function signature mismatch' on frame #1. DISCARDED.

BROKEN — trapped 'unreachable' on frame #1, even though this instruments MORE functions than the shipped build. This is the definitive result: IGNORE_INDIRECT is not repairable by any add-list here, because it removes the machinery for unwinding THROUGH an indirect call site regardless of which functions are instrumented. Per the ADVISE ground truth above that is the emulation closure — effectively all 1212 minus the ~60 non-emulation entries, i.e. it converges on the remove-list variant below, with strictly more risk and no extra upside.

WORKS — ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED over 300 frames, 2.6% smaller, but 0% faster (34.68 vs 34.91 is inside the ~2% noise band). NOT SHIPPED: Emscripten's own documentation warns a remove-list can break on code paths that were never exercised during testing, and for a frame-perfect TAS tool there is no speed upside to justify that risk. The list is kept at /projects/bsnes-mercury/asyncify-remove.txt and is opt-in via EMS_ASYNCIFY_EXTRA='-s ASYNCIFY_REMOVE=@asyncify-remove.txt'.

asyncify_pruning_rejected.conclusion: Asyncify instrumentation is NOT the accuracy profile's bottleneck, and no correct pruning of it is available. Pruning could remove at most 30% of module SIZE (1,836,962 -> 1,289,761 B) and every configuration that actually achieved that broke the core. The real cost is the ~39,436 fiber swaps per frame — see measurements.why_accuracy_barely_moved.

makefile_edits: The upstream emscripten platform block emitted only an intermediate LLVM bitcode archive (.bc). It performs the full Emscripten link to <profile>.js + .wasm with CC=emcc/CXX=em++/LD=em++, STATIC_LINKING=0, and the raw-libretro flag set (ALLOW_TABLE_GROWTH, exported runtime methods incl. addFunction, exported retro_*). Earlier passes added: (1) -s ASYNCIFY=1 + ASYNCIFY_STACK_SIZE so retro_run yields to the browser and returns instead of hanging in bsnes's libco scheduler; (2) per-PROFILE DISTINCT output filename + MODULARIZE EXPORT_NAME (bsnes_accuracy / bsnes_balanced / bsnes_performance) so the cores can coexist without a symbol collision; (3) -s EXPORT_ES6=1 so each core is an ES6 default-export factory that core-loader.js resolves via dynamic import. THIS pass added overridable optimization knobs (EMS_OPT, EMS_LINK_OPT, EMS_SIMD, EMS_DEBUG_OFF, EMS_CLOSURE, EMS_INITIAL_MEMORY, EMS_STACK_SIZE, EMS_ASYNCIFY_STACK_SIZE, EMS_ASYNCIFY_EXTRA — all `?=` so variants can be measured from the command line) and wired EMS_LINK_OPT/EMS_SIMD/EMS_DEBUG_OFF/EMS_CLOSURE into the SHARED link flag set, which is what fixed the -O0 link.
libco_backend_edit: libco defaults to the sjlj (setjmp/longjmp) backend under Emscripten, whose raw-stack context switches ASYNCIFY cannot unwind (retro_run hang). Added libco/emscripten.c, an Emscripten Fibers (emscripten_fiber_*) libco backend, and wired it in libco/libco.c under the __EMSCRIPTEN__ target so cothread switches cooperate with ASYNCIFY. This pass additionally added an OPTIONAL, #ifdef-guarded swap counter (-DLIBCO_SWAP_COUNTER exports libco_swap_count/libco_swap_count_reset) used to measure fiber swaps per frame. It is off by default and the shipped cores are byte-identical with the guard present.
verified_with: For ALL THREE profiles: node tools/run-smoke.mjs cores/<profile>.js 300 — retro_load_game()==true, retro_run() RETURNS for all 300 frames (no hang), video_refresh fires with a non-null framebuffer of plausible SNES width, the frame counter advances, ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED. Plus node tools/core-probe.mjs for the raw retro_* ABI + addFunction, and the full tools/ suite (cd tools && npm test).

noasyncify_experiment.goal: Test whether bsnes-mercury accuracy can run WITHOUT ASYNCIFY (a smaller, faster core) inside a Web Worker, since a worker thread blocking is acceptable (it does not freeze the UI). The user specifically asked to try -s SUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm and native fiber switching for libco cothreads.

noasyncify_experiment.libco_backend_tried: The Emscripten Fibers backend (libco/emscripten.c) is implemented ON TOP OF Asyncify (emscripten_fiber_* require -s ASYNCIFY), so it cannot be used in a no-ASYNCIFY build. libco.c was taught to fall back to the sjlj (setjmp/longjmp) backend under __EMSCRIPTEN__ when LIBCO_NO_ASYNCIFY is defined, relying on -s SUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm so longjmp uses Wasm exception handling. (Makefile NOASYNCIFY=1 variant + libco/libco.c LIBCO_NO_ASYNCIFY guard, both in the /projects/bsnes-mercury source tree, additive + gated so the shipping ASYNCIFY build is unchanged.)
noasyncify_experiment.build_result: COMPILED + LINKED cleanly. .wasm was ~1.6 MB (vs ~3.7 MB for the then-current unoptimized ASYNCIFY build). Loaded fine: retro_load_game()==true, av_info 256x224 @ 60.099 fps, WRAM ptr+size present.
noasyncify_experiment.run_smoke_result: HUNG/THREW — FAIL. The very FIRST retro_run() threw a WebAssembly.Exception immediately — 0 frames advanced, 0 video_refresh calls. Root cause: libco's sjlj backend swaps cothreads via sigaltstack/raise(SIGUSR1)/sigsetjmp/siglongjmp, which do not perform a real stack switch under WASM; SUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm only rewrites C longjmp into a Wasm-EH throw, so the cothread 'switch' unwinds as an exception out of retro_run instead of transferring control to the CPU/PPU cothread.
noasyncify_experiment.decision: FELL BACK. Did NOT ship a no-ASYNCIFY bsnes core. ASYNCIFY + Emscripten Fibers remains the only working configuration for bsnes.
noasyncify_experiment.note_after_optimization_pass: Its headline '~1.6 MB vs ~3.7 MB, therefore ASYNCIFY is the bloat' inference was misleading, because the 3.7 MB figure came from the broken -O0 LINK. With the link fixed, the ASYNCIFY accuracy core is 1.80 MB, so ASYNCIFY's true size cost is roughly 0.5 MB (an ASYNCIFY_IGNORE_INDIRECT build, though functionally broken, measured 1.29 MB), not 2.1 MB.
